fixes.answer: While there are many pressing issues, I believe climate change is arguably the most significant, because it threatens the very [[habitability]] of our planet and amplifies other problems like poverty and conflict. Its effects are global and potentially irreversible. That said, inequality and the risks of new technology are also profound. So although I would single out climate change as the most urgent and [[far-reaching]], these challenges are deeply [[interconnected]].

For many modern challenges, international cooperation is not just preferable but essential. Problems like climate change, pandemics and terrorism [[do not respect borders]], so no single country can solve them alone. While nations should certainly address their domestic issues, the great [[transnational]] challenges require collective, coordinated action. So I would argue that in an interconnected world, a spirit of cooperation and shared responsibility is [[indispensable]] for tackling our common threats.
fixes.why: 'cooperation' and 'responsibility' are plain; marked 'do not respect borders' and 'indispensable'

fixes.answer: The difficulty largely stems from competing national interests and a lack of trust. Countries are often reluctant to bear costs or make sacrifices, especially if they fear others will not do the same. Differing priorities between rich and poor nations complicate matters, and there is no single global authority to enforce agreements. Short-term political thinking also gets in the way. So global problems persist because collective action requires overcoming [[deep-seated]] [[self-interest]] and [[coordination failures]].
fixes.why: 4 marks with 'failures' split; marked 'deep-seated' and the phrase 'coordination failures'

fixes.answer: Global problems have very real and personal impacts, even when they seem distant. Climate change brings extreme weather that destroys homes and livelihoods. A global pandemic, as we have seen, can [[upend]] everyone's daily life and health. Economic crises that originate elsewhere can cause job losses locally. So although these issues are global in scale, their consequences are felt [[intimately]] in ordinary people's [[livelihoods]], health and security, which is why they matter to us all.

I try to remain cautiously optimistic, despite the [[daunting]] challenges. History shows that humanity is remarkably capable of innovation and cooperation when truly pressed, and we have overcome major threats before. Growing global awareness and technological progress offer real hope. However, success is far from guaranteed and will require unprecedented political will. So while I acknowledge the risks are serious, I choose to believe in human [[ingenuity]] and our capacity to [[rise to the occasion]].
fixes.why: 'rise' is part of an idiom; marked 'daunting' and the full idiom 'rise to the occasion'

fixes.answer: Strengthening international institutions and agreements is essential, giving them more authority to coordinate and, where necessary, enforce collective action. Building trust between nations through dialogue and fair [[burden-sharing]] is crucial, ensuring poorer countries are supported. Aligning short-term incentives with long-term goals would help too. Ultimately, fostering a genuine sense of [[shared humanity]] and common purpose, over [[narrow nationalism]], is the foundation of effective cooperation.
fixes.why: 'purpose' and 'cooperation' are plain and 'cooperation' repeated; marked 'burden-sharing', 'shared humanity', 'narrow nationalism'

fixes.answer: The advantages of our interconnected world are immense: the [[free flow of ideas]], trade and technology, cultural exchange, and the ability to cooperate on shared problems. It has driven progress and [[lifted many from poverty]]. The disadvantages are that problems, whether financial crises, pandemics or misinformation, also spread rapidly across borders, making us more [[vulnerable]]. So interconnection brings both tremendous opportunity and shared vulnerability, which we must learn to manage wisely.
fixes.why: 'opportunity' is plain and 'vulnerability' repeats 'vulnerable'; marked 'free flow of ideas' and 'lifted many from poverty'

fixes.answer: I respectfully disagree, as I find this view [[unduly disempowering]]. While it is true that individuals cannot [[single-handedly]] solve global problems, collective individual action is precisely what drives change. Our consumer choices, our activism, and above all our votes shape the policies of governments and the behaviour of corporations. Great social movements have always begun with ordinary people. So while one person's impact is small, collectively individuals [[wield]] genuine influence and should not underestimate it.
